title: Stone Points From Arabia May Have Carried Poison
paragraphs: About 125,000 years ago, a freshwater lake lay in what is now the Empty Quarter desert in Saudi Arabia. Many animals came to the water, and so did people.

Scientists studied the place, called 'Uruq Aljelibah. They found more than 5,000 stone tools next to fossils of animals such as hippos, camels and oryx. Some stone points were fixed to shafts with plant glue and fibres, so they were made from several materials.
Some points also had chemical traces from a tree used for arrow poison. The team says people may have used poison, but this is not proven.
